references.text: The Pharisees worry that the whole world will follow after Jesus, a direct consequence of the many signs mentioned in John 11:47.

Caiaphas' argument at the Sanhedrin meeting that it is better for one man to die for the people is the direct logical conclusion to the question in John 11:47 about what they should do regarding the man's signs.
The chief priests and Pharisees gather again to plan Jesus' death, a repetition of the meeting in John 11:47 where they worried about his signs.
The chief priests and scribes look for a way to take Jesus' life, inspired by fear of his signs and influence, just as in John 11:47.
